## Design

### 2026-10-14 – Today, I started work on BLOXX, specifically the base of it, which is the drawer (called "box" in the repo), and the casing for it. (casing in repo) I took inspiration from PlayConveyor's design, and

**4h**

Today, I started work on BLOXX, specifically the base of it, which is the drawer (called "box" in the repo), and the casing for it. (casing in repo) I took inspiration from PlayConveyor's design, and I decided to make that, but with more customization and utility. (also you can mount it on the floor but that's not too important.

PlayConveyor's design:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/c4c499da7a5e47336f5ae207b51c9887249a5db6a005e690c5f9412d1e511cb7.png)

First I began work on the base. I do have some experience with Onshape, so I decided to use that. I created a hollow, 5x5 square, and added "rails" to the side, which it would slide upon to reveal it's contents, and 2 springy, interlocking triangles, which took some... convincing.

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 224324](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/a24f979249ac0e55ae6c3436ac783bb0b8946d1211063a2571004cf70843a9f5.png)

 The triangles are there so that you can just shove the drawer into the base to assemble it. Also some label text as a quality-of-life feature.

The base:

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 225835](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/219c12990d11b1c78e2695619fe011c531b69e5790bd0a33a0d7f0b8f799a806.png)

Next I began work on the case, which is harder, since you have to try to kind of create the negative of what you have already, while making a convenient user experience. It's not finished, but the idea is there. On the sides I'm planning some kind of "snapping" system in order to connect 2 bases together.

![image_2026-10-14_000702508](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/dde6d55d011b273498d1261c44c6bc57cba2d1f2f7c45bce4b1237bb9303e449.png)

I have to complete the case and then the actual base it will attach to, so that mounting is possible, and then we can start work on some of the more "exciting" features, like cabinets, customization, etc.

### 2026-10-15 – #Day 2 - Finalizing the case#

**4h**

#Day 2 - Finalizing the case#

As you can probably tell, most of the work on this project was trying to finish the case mounting system.
First, I tried to finish up what I needed to. Putting the drawer rails on both sides of the case, fixing up the box cutouts so that they align on both sides, and looking up / thinking about rail designs.

The new box:

![image_2026-10-14_234143140](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/e22cae12aba99d6c0e01466a02d2da5e55ef80438aa063eb4c5ab547c55e5e07.png)

Next, I attempted to create a rail system for the casing, so you can attach one casing to another. For reference, you put the drawer inside the "casing" and then the casing latch on to another, creating modularity, along with a triangle to secure it in place. This process was pretty time consuming, but I learned a lot of things along the way, like how to copy/paste in Onshape, and how to make objects of the same sketch different layers.

My CAD-induced nightmare (putting the system on both sides):

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 223727](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/4baf7743f50ab3e61231252db75414e7d836b3cce703746528219dfae2452962.png)

I then pasted the same rail system on the other side, and I was done, before I realized... Wait, how are they going to connect? On the other side of the model, I created a negative of the rails, so you can slide one on the side of the other.

Me working on the rail system and then realizing:
![Screenshot 2026-10-14 232551](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/c4316323de332e34bf5fc90af68339f980d65ad16f7f8034130ba9ca29b43e29.png)

Now I want to talk about where this project is going to go. Right now, you can only connect them in one direction, so I want to improve on this rail system, also making it go up and down. Next is mounting plates, but after the base is done, everything else is easier because you know how things will work later. I want to create a workable format for myself to follow.

My current progress:

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 233809](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/7e514d1f34eb780e703a7e52f1180adbe2f00881e784651093906ea370a547ff.png)

### 2026-10-16 – #Week 2 Day 4 - Downfall#

**4h**

#Week 2 Day 4 - Downfall#

Today, I finished the casing and the way they mount to each other. I'm using a  rail system so that you can slide one onto another, once again like Play Conveyor's. On one side is the exact negative of the other, I don't know how to really describe it. The picture helps. I added rails to the top and bottom so that you can mount one on another, making them stackable. We already have a modular system.

Me working on it:

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 205025](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/04e76bc2a9eff42bf9e80793454edf59ced92c82965c10bf934f5d4161752159.png)

Final case design:

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 215156](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/f5a52989c8f36265adf23d58b0bba41e5effa0feb4776eeabf9d0941a60a7d25.png)

I then began work on the base, which is where the cases attach to, in order for floor or wall mounting. There's not much about them to say, but what there is to say, is that they have the rail system on the bottom, so you can mount the cases on them, and then puzzle-piece styled outlines allows you to connect one to the other.

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 230816](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/01b1229046696cd47a202a10e9938a9e80247d8774502488cc994932bf7e812e.png)

Finally, when I put them into the assembly tab, I noticed some problems. Mainly how some bits of geometry would fall off. That's where the Boolean tool came in. I unified all the parts until they were each one part that I could cleanly import into the assembly. Then came the assembly. I assembled all the parts,  made it so that all the slider mates went the correct way, and then I ended up with a successful mockup!

The mockup, in all it's glory:
![Screenshot 2026-10-15 233643](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/c0061eb828af1edbea29a116a3990a459b140e03b8685318e96bfb75060dec29.png)

However, as I finished the mockup I noticed some problems. The little holes where the rails went were too far apart, and in real life they wouldn't successfully connect up. Along with this, the base pieces were aligned in such a way that I would need to confirm that the base pieces would actually fit between them correctly, not too close, not too far. Finally, I need to add some clearance between the gaps. A 3d printer will not perfectly make the gaps and tolerances between the rails, so I'd make the connector rail "holes" a bit bigger than they need to, just in order so that all printers are accommodated. I need to go through **CAD HELL** to fix these issues, and I might not have enough time to make the additional features, but in my opinion, it would be worth it, because having 3 functional features that interact with each other is better than having 15 that barely work and don't work with each other.

### 2026-10-17 – ##Day 4 (Sorry, my bad, the last entry was day 3) Adding additional features##

**4h**

##Day 4 (Sorry, my bad, the last entry was day 3) Adding additional features##

Today was a busy day. I picked up from last time where I said I was going to fix the existing features and try to add new ones if possible. Surprisingly, Onshape was feeling nice today, and it wasn't so hard to fix any of them. I started by making sure that the tiles didn't interfere with the connections of the casings. I sized them down about 0.2 inches before I saw that they were matching up. YES!

Tile lineup:
![Screenshot 2026-10-16 201333](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/25a35556b4462ee941c24d3f49a026a8771d1a70717fbfd0b17ca30e03d5d94c.png)

Next, I fit the drawer to the actual box, which was WAYYYY easier than expected. It was just a matter of shrinking down a sketch, and moving the rails accordingly. The drawer now fits like a glove into the casing, and everything else is compliant.

Fitting pieces:
![Screenshot 2026-10-16 212810](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/83794aa89a21a248954e6ccdae1c8338b965cc72b2662c94b36320bdd835b82c.png)

Finally, tolerances.  I sized up some holes about 0.03 inches bigger, which should definitely be enough for any 3d printer now.

Now, we move onto the new features. I added a 1x2 box, which is VERY easy to make, since everything just works and fits nicely, since I designed the model to be modular. I knew that making a modular system would benefit in the future, because now it's super easy to add new systems and features to the existing base.

1x2 box:

![Screenshot 2026-10-16 224621](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/eaac71a76e0d3b48b64e8bf7229ed6b008cce4229ce4f4471ae9f6d7f456c750.png)

However, the same CANNOT be said for the casing. This model had so many separate parts and jank that it was very hard to scale it up. The rail systems had to be designed again, and it was just a very time consuming process overall, trying to adapt it for 2 "puzzle pieces" instead of one, and making sure it will actually work. I'm still not done with the model, but very close. I should take my time adjusting the  configuration, because once again I would rather ship with 3 working features that can interact with each other than 15 that don't work and cannot interact with each other.

Casing:

![Screenshot 2026-10-16 223949](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/b2753e27a0a428729fc7d4d8dd7dba72a2b313c1dbc6ee82b33439340cb4a0df.png)

Finally, what's next?  After this I will just add the closet module, Gridfinity-compatible shelves and drawers,  some basic customization, and a guide on how to make your own, then it's just finishing the repo and polish.
